acceptance_criteria.requirement: The dashboard is at most 1240px wide with at least 16px side margins, 22px top spacing, 12-14px major gaps, and 66px of bottom clearance for 42px native controls plus a 24px gap.
At 1040px and wider the calendar and a right rail remain side by side, with the rail at least 372px wide and its metric cards top-aligned.
From 420px through 1039px the calendar, auto-fitting metric grid with an approximately 180px minimum card width, and Bible card stack in that order.
Below 420px the calendar footer uses three readable rows, the metric cards use one column, content remains vertically scrollable, and cards do not clip.

At 480px and above the full Year has no horizontal scrolling; below 480px only the approximately 580px-wide Year heatmap may scroll, with 12px edge padding, a restrained 5px scrollbar, and subtle edge fades.
Year height remains content-driven and independent of Bible disabled, short, and long states.
Five-row Month views remain naturally shorter than six-row views without forcing equal calendar heights.

Year remains one continuous 53-column presentation with aligned month labels, January and December fully reachable, initial or explicit-Today centering on the current month, and preserved manual scroll position across rerenders.
Completed reviews own cell fill, future cells stay neutral, and due demand uses only the three-level bottom-strip treatment.
Outside-month, future, completion, due, event, today, selected, hover, and focus states follow one deterministic visual and keyboard layering order.
Events use compact gold markers approximately 5px from the top and right edges, multiple events use a separate count badge, and markers never overlap dates.
The legend uses Completed reviews with Low and High endpoints, three matching Reviews due samples, and one Event marker.
One delegated 190-220px tooltip flips and shifts within the calendar and viewport, avoids the source cell where possible, and works in Month and Year.
Month and Year form one segmented control; previous, Today, and next form a second cohesive group with a separate settings control.

The footer divides date, event, and action regions; it uses one row at 760px and above, two rows from 420px through 759px, and three rows below 420px, while long localized dates wrap instead of clipping.

The footer says Next event for Today, On this date for a selected date with an event, and No event on this date otherwise; its action switches between Add event and Edit event while Reviewed and Due actions cannot displace the date or event title.
Today progress is one readable completion bar containing N% complete across both filled and unfilled portions, never a segmented workload visualization.
No cards scheduled, All clear, 100% complete, and unavailable are distinct states; no unavailable state invents a percentage.
Today’s Progress contains New remaining, Learning remaining, Reviews remaining, and Total remaining.
Today’s Session contains Cards studied, New cards studied, Cards buried, Time spent, Pace, and ETA.
Cards buried remains the scheduler-authoritative current total, has no historical analytics, and visibility.buried is removed.
Last 7 Days contains Cards studied, New cards studied, Retention, and Again rate.
All Time contains Avg cards/day, Current streak, Longest streak, Retention, and Cards studied.
Wide metric labels remain on one line at or above the supplied typography minimums; tabular right-aligned values stay stable and time or ETA uses compact readable copy when necessary.
Initial Python rendering and live JavaScript updates consume the same progress, session, time, and footer presentation contract.
A new profile uses deliberate empty-history treatment with No cards scheduled and N/A rates rather than looking partially broken.
Historical all-clear and completed-positive-workload states remain visually and semantically distinct, including ETA Done only for completed positive work.
Bible height is content-driven, long text is not truncated below 14px, custom font affects verse text only, and disabled state leaves no gap.
All palettes derive from centralized thematic and semantic tokens; Graphite interactions use its slate accent family while semantic blue remains reserved for New cards.
Only Sapphire Glass uses component-level 94-100 opacity and real 0-16px backdrop blur.
Emerald Dark uses page #0B1210, card #101B17, raised card #14231C, empty cell #17251F, subtle border #294137, and accent #3CCF8E; Graphite and Emerald surfaces remain opaque.
High Contrast uses opaque crisp surfaces with no decorative transparency or shadows.
The add-on never creates, recolors, masks, blurs, or scrims the host wallpaper, native deck list, toolbar, footer, or surrounding Anki canvas.
Schema 8 clamps schema-7 opacity and blur, defaults to 96 and 12, removes visibility.buried, preserves unrelated settings, and disables glass controls outside Sapphire.
A valid stored Month or Year value loads before first render, changes only on explicit user selection, and is reused for loading, refresh, retry, theme, settings save, and restart.
Initial and delayed loading reserve the selected Month or Year geometry, use clearly visible skeletons, and say Still loading your study data... without changing dimensions.
Initial failure uses an approximately 400-440px panel with 20px padding and 32px Retry plus Open diagnostics actions, without a fake zero snapshot.

Refresh or retry with prior data keeps that dashboard visible, shows Refreshing..., then exposes exactly one full-width failure banner containing one last_updated_at timestamp without discarding the last successful data.
The 1.8.3 archive is built once and verifies version, the 24-member allowlist, safe paths, successful loading, and byte-for-byte source parity.

The exact archive runs in one fresh sync-disabled Anki 26.8 profile with one restart, produces 55 initial frames plus RUNTIME-RESTART-PERSISTENCE, one overview and 15 detail sheets, and restart persistence has no waiver.

The supplied screenshot and retained 1.8.0/1.8.1/1.8.2 evidence remain unchanged calibration history; VoiceOver, forced colors, Windows/Linux, non-100% scaling, and OS scaling stay explicitly deferred and unclaimed.
